title: Safe Water for Rural Schools
key_sentences: In 2025 the initiative completed 42 new boreholes and rehabilitated 14 older wells across thirteen districts, bringing safe drinking water to an estimated 32,700 people.
Construction costs per borehole fell by 12 percent compared with the previous year, mainly because drilling teams were shared between neighbouring districts.
Each site was surveyed by a hydrogeologist before any equipment was moved.
Committees collect a small monthly fee that pays for spare parts and for the caretaker's time.
Hygiene clubs were set up in 26 primary schools.
A water point counts as functional when it delivered water on the day of the inspection.
Administrative costs remained below the ceiling of 10 percent set by the board.
The initiative will also test solar-powered pumps at four schools where the water table is deeper than 60 metres.
